import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Parse the date column
data['Dt_Customer'] = pd.to_datetime(data['Dt_Customer'], format='%d-%m-%Y')

# Calculate the total amount spent by each customer
data['Total_Spent'] = data['MntWines'] + data['MntFruits'] + data['MntMeatProducts'] + \
                      data['MntFishProducts'] + data['MntSweetProducts'] + data['MntGoldProds']

# Group by Education and Marital Status, and calculate the average income and total spent
grouped_data = data.groupby(['Education', 'Marital_Status']).agg({
    'Income': 'mean',
    'Total_Spent': 'mean'
}).reset_index()

# Set up the matplotlib figure
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create the bar plot
sns.barplot(x='Education', y='Total_Spent', hue='Marital_Status', data=grouped_data, palette='muted')

# Add labels and title
plt.title('Average Total Spending by Education and Marital Status')
plt.xlabel('Education Level')
plt.ylabel('Average Total Spending')
plt.legend(title='Marital Status', loc='upper left')

# Save the plot
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd

    'Income': 'mean',
    'Total_Spent': 'mean'
}).reset_index()

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
